Render an HTML briefing for one force or council

Source: R/profile.R
btg_report.Rd

Writes a self-contained HTML briefing from the package's installed R Markdown template: the headline statements of btg_profile(), the ranking, robustness, trend and change charts for the area, the tables behind them, reporting coverage, the methods and their limits, and the citation and release identifiers needed to reproduce every figure.

Usage

btg_report(
  force = NULL,
  council = NULL,
  year = NULL,
  release = NULL,
  file,
  format = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  draws = 2000L,
  seed = 1L
)

Arguments

force

A Police.uk force identifier such as "metropolitan", or

council

an ONS local-authority code such as "E09000022". Name one of the two.

year

The calendar year to profile. NULL uses the latest year the source covers in full.

release

A value from btg_releases(); NULL uses the default catalogue release.

file

Path of the file to write.

format

"html" for a self-contained web page, "docx" for a Word document or "pdf" for a PDF, all with the same content. NULL takes the format from the file's extension.

overwrite

Whether to replace an existing file.

draws, seed

Simulation settings passed to btg_rank_stability().

Value

The path of the written file, invisibly.

Details

Rendering needs the rmarkdown package and Pandoc, which RStudio and Positron supply, and a PDF additionally needs a LaTeX installation such as TinyTeX (tinytex::install_tinytex()); the function stops with a clear message when any is missing. Paragraphs are justified and the body text is 12-point Calibri in HTML and Word; the PDF uses Calibri too, through XeLaTeX, when the machine has that font or its open counterpart Carlito, and LaTeX's default face otherwise. Tables are set with btg_table(), Word output uses the styled reference document installed with the template, and PDF output uses booktabs tables. Charts in a briefing carry only their coverage note, because the briefing states the sources and qualifications itself; the option BlackThriveSS.caption = "short" does the same for any chart. Figures are drawn at page width, as vector graphics in PDF and at print resolution in Word, on A4 pages. The template is also available in those editors as the R Markdown template "BlackThriveSS briefing" for editing, where Knit to HTML, Word or PDF gives the same three outputs.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("rmarkdown", quietly = TRUE) && rmarkdown::pandoc_available("2.0")) {
  path <- tempfile(fileext = ".html")
  btg_report(force = "metropolitan", file = path, draws = 500)
  unlink(path)
}
# }
